title: Autonomous operation and maintenance of ISRU plants
bottleneck: An ISRU plant must run for years with no crew present — handling abrasive dust, extreme temperatures, and corrosive chemistry while diagnosing and repairing its own faults. Terrestrial chemical plants have maintenance crews; a lunar plant gets none, and teleoperation from Earth suffers 2.6-second delays that make fine manipulation impractical. Self-repairing robotics, fault-tolerant design, and in-situ spare-part manufacturing are all immature, and a single unrecoverable fault can strand a multi-billion-dollar asset.
why_it_blocks: ISRU must produce propellant before crews arrive — that is the whole point; without autonomy, the plant needs a crew, which needs the propellant: a circular dependency.
current_state: Terrestrial mining automation is advanced but assumes human servicing; space-rated autonomous chemical processing has never been demonstrated.
